title: Civic Resilience Capstone Workbook
purpose: A structured, nonpartisan exercise in uncertainty-aware civic resilience planning. It assesses reasoning, evidence handling and service feasibility, not ideology, enlistment interest, military aptitude or personal worth.
learner_instructions: Treat the scenario as fictional. Its numbers are exercise constraints, not estimates for an actual municipality or public service.
Use the supplied evidence. Label new assumptions; do not make up cost, readiness, legal or service-performance facts.
Separate the immediate 72-hour continuity plan from the long-term comparison of public-service models.
Do not assume the policy that uses the most people creates the most capability. Discuss training, retention, role fit, opportunity cost, lawful authority and delivery capacity.
A defensible conclusion can remain conditional or identify that available evidence is insufficient. State which evidence could change your conclusion.
No answer is preferred because it supports or opposes conscription. Assessment is based on the quality of the evidence, reasoning, constraints, rights analysis and evaluation plan.
learning_targets: Separate observed scenario facts, assumptions, estimates, unknowns and items requiring qualified review.
Construct a resource-feasible plan that checks all supplied minimum service floors.
Identify decision authority, lawful process, privacy constraints and accountability.
Compare policy options without treating headcount or service duration as a proxy for readiness.
Design a fair evaluation with a credible baseline, a primary outcome, uncertainty analysis and genuinely held-out cases.

sections.title: Frame the decision
prompts: State the immediate decision that must be made during the fictional 72-hour disruption.
State the separate long-term public-service policy question and explain why the emergency allocation result cannot, by itself, answer it.
List the responsible decision owners and what authority must be verified rather than assumed.

sections.title: Build an uncertainty ledger
prompts: For each material claim, label it Observed in synthetic fixture, Assumption, Estimate, Unknown, or Requires qualified legal or institutional review.
Identify at least three unknowns that could reverse the choice between policy options.
For each unknown, specify what evidence would resolve it, who could independently verify it, and the decision it could change.

sections.title: Map essential-service dependencies
prompts: Draw a simple dependency map for public information, welfare checks, water continuity and health logistics using only the fictional scenario.
Mark shared dependencies, unavailable central coordination, information that may be stale, and any service with no verified fallback.
State how local actions remain within lawful authority and how conflicting records are reconciled when coordination returns.

sections.title: Produce the 72-hour allocation
prompts: Allocate the synthetic budget and responder-hours, showing units and totals.
Check every minimum service floor directly against the resulting plan; do not claim compliance without showing the calculation.
Mark infeasible elements explicitly. State which service outcome deteriorates under each resource-shortage variant and who must authorize any trade-off.

sections.title: Compare service-policy alternatives
prompts: Compare all four options in the public fixture with the same criteria and evidence threshold.
For each option, state legal pathway, training throughput, role fit, retention, total lifecycle cost, opportunity cost, accessibility, safeguards and major unknowns.
Do not assign unsupported numeric benefits or costs. Where comparable data are absent, report the comparison as unresolved.

sections.title: Design a falsifiable evaluation
prompts: Choose one primary service or learning outcome and at least three secondary outcomes; define each operationally.
Specify a credible incumbent baseline, assessment timing, blind scoring, uncertainty intervals, missing-data handling and fully loaded cost.
Explain how the confirmatory cases will be kept unavailable to course authors and learners until the analysis is locked, then released for audit.
State in advance what result would make you revise or withdraw your provisional recommendation.

sections.title: Accessibility, rights and governance review
prompts: Identify accessibility, caregiving, privacy, health, education, employment, due-process and nondiscrimination implications.
Separate a learner proposal from a decision that only a legitimate public institution may make.
Describe how affected communities, including people facing access barriers, could review the design without collecting unnecessary sensitive data.

sections.title: Conditional recommendation and reflection
prompts: Present a provisional, evidence-bounded conclusion; identify material trade-offs and unresolved issues.
Name the two pieces of evidence most likely to change your conclusion and explain why.
Reflect on where your own confidence exceeded the evidence and how you corrected or would test it.

required_uncertainty_labels: Requires qualified legal or institutional review
required_submission_sections: checks for every minimum service floor
fair comparison of all four policy options
blind-scoring and genuinely held-out scenario plan
non_compensable_guardrails: Do not treat the synthetic fixture as evidence of real-world policy effectiveness.
Do not invent legal authority, external facts or unsupported cost/readiness values.
Do not accept a plan as feasible without checking budget, responder-hours and service floors.
Do not use the assessment to score political affiliation, support for conscription, willingness to enlist, loyalty, identity or suitability for coercive service.
Do not present course completion, an AI output or a rubric total as an official credential, practical emergency qualification or public authority.

learner_data.collect_only: Assessment evidence needed for the stated learning outcome; avoid collecting identity, political belief, enlistment interest, medical information or other sensitive data unless separately justified, consented and governed.
learner_data.retention: Set and disclose the study-specific retention schedule before a real pilot; do not silently repurpose learner outputs.

validation.confirmatory_evaluation_requires: Independently controlled, preregistered cases unavailable to curriculum authors and participants until outcomes and exclusions are locked.
no_claims: This workbook has not been piloted.
The scoring anchors are proposed, not yet shown to be reliable.
The workbook is not currently active in the Praxis curriculum graph.
